la:verb:inveho.gloss: to carry, bear, convey into, introduce, bring in, bring upon
senses: to carry, bear, convey into, introduce, bring in, bring upon
to ride, drive, sally, fly to or into
to attack, assail, fall upon, assault
to attack with words, inveigh against
la:verb:inveho.html:
in-vĕho, vexi, vectum, 3, v. a.,
to carry, bear, or bring to or into a place, in one's hands, on a horse, by water, etc.
Lit.
Act.
With in and acc.: tantum in aerarium pecuniae invexit, ut,: Euphrates in Mesopotamiam quasi novos agros invehit,.—
With acc. of place (poet., except with names of towns, etc.): marmor Romam,; : Iamque mare (lyra et lingua) invectae flumen relinquunt,. —
With dat.: Caesar legiones per flumen Oceano invexit,: gazam urbi,: quas (opes) mare litoribus invehit,. —
Absol. (sc. frumenta), into the barns, : peregrinas mercis,. —
Pass.
To ride, drive, sail, fly to or into a place: dictator triumphans urbem invehitur,i. e. enters,; ; : invecta corpori patris nefando vehiculo filia,: at Caesar triplici invectus Romano triumpho moenia,: invehitur celeri barbarus hostis equo,; cf.: equitum acies invecta in dissipatos,; so ; : equo,; ; : curru,: invectus mare,carried into the sea,: in portum ex alto invehi,; : portum invectus,; cf.: ab invectis portum audit,. —With dat.: classes invectas Tibridis alveo,; : ostio fluminis,.—
To enter, penetrate: cum utrimque invehi hostem nunciaretur,: Alexander ordines . . . multa caede hostium invehitur,.—
Invehere se, or invehi, to attack, assail, fall upon, assault; to force one's way in, penetrate.—With se: invehebant se hostes,; : cum eo ipso acrius victores se undique inveherent,. — Pass.: Valerius temere invectus in aciem,; equites in laevum cornu invecti sunt,; ; : belua invehebatur ordinibus,: levi agmine,: currus in phalangem invecti erant, et saep.—
Trop.
Act., to introduce, bring in, bring upon: quae (mala) tibi casus invexerit,: partem incommodorum,: ut quemcumque casum fortuna invexerit,brings with it,: divitiae avaritiam invexere, Liv. praef. § 12.—
Pass., to attack with words, inveigh against: in homines caros,: quod consul in eum ordinem essct invectus,: acerbius in aliquem, id, Lael. 16, 57: in adversarios,; : in Philotam,: aliquid inclementius in te,: vehementius in causam principum,: in eam artem,.— Act.: * de quo Caesar in senatu aperte in te invehens questus est,.— With Gr. acc.: cum nonnulla inveheretur in Timoleonta,: multa in Thebanos,. — Hence, invectus, a, um, P. a., brought in: invecta et illata (or without et): invecta illata, things brought into a house by the tenant, i. e. his movables, household stuff, furniture: placet, in urbanis habitationibus locandis, invecta illata, pignori esse locatori, : invecta et illata pignori erunt obligata,.

la:verb:invito.html:
invīto, āvi, ātum, 1 (invitassitis for invitaveritis, ), v. a.
perh. for invicito; root vec-; Sanscr. vak-, speak; vak'as, word; cf.: vox, convicium; Gr. ϝεπ- in εἶπον, ὄψ
,
to invite, treat, feast, entertain (cf. illicio; class.).
Lit., constr. with ad or in and acc., with simple acc. or abl., or with ut.
With ad: aliquem ad prandium,: ad cenam,; ; ; ad consulem,—
With in and acc.: aliquem in hospitium,; cf. , ext. 1: ad cenam in hortos in posterum diem,. —
With simple acc.: aliquem domum suam ut animum ejus in Sthenium inflammarent (cf. ε infra), ; : alius alium domos suas invitant,. 3; .—
With abl.: aliquem tecto ac domo,; cf.: hospitio invitabit,.— (ε) With ut: invito eum, ut apud me diversetur,; ut cenem invitor?.— Absol., to entertain: alii suos in castra, invitandi causā adducunt,: aliquem poculis,to challenge to drink,. — With se, to treat one's self, drink one's

own health: sese in cena plusculum,: se cibo vinoque largius, ap. (Hist. 4, 4 Dietsch). —Comic.: gladio, to treat to the sword, i. e. to want to kill, ; cf.: aliquem clavā,.—

Transf.
To invite, summon, challenge: a Caesare liberaliter invitor in legationem illam,: Cosconio mortuo, in ejus locum invitor,: hostes ad deditionem,: aliquem ad audiendum,: ad spectaculum,: praemiis ad quippiam agendum,: in libidinem,.—
To incite, allure, attract: ni id me invitet ut faciam fides,: invitat hiemps curasque resolvit,: invitent croceis halantes floribus horti,: ad agrum fruendum invitat atque allectat senectus,; so, assentationem,to encourage flattery,: invitare et allicere appetitum animi,: somnos,to attract,: culpam,to allure to transgression,: invitatur vino appetentia ciborum,: fossis invitavit mare,i. e. conducted,. — Trop., of things: invitat somnos crepitantibus unda lapillis,; cf. . — With inf.: vicina invitet decedere ripa calori,.—
To ask, request, urge: Germanos, uti ab Rheno discederent,: benignis verbis, ut, etc.,

la:adj:invidiosus.html:
invĭdĭōsus, a, um, adj.
invidia
.
Full of envy, envious, invidious, hostile (i. q. invidus; class.): illa peraeque Prae se formosis invidiosa dea est, (3, 24, 10): vetustas,.—
Enviable: possessiones,; cf. : pecunia,; so, nec curis erat (Pactolus) invidiosus harenis,by reason of,; cf.: invidiosior mors,; and in a good sense,: spes procorum,desired, longed for,; : praemia,: solacia,.—
Exciting envy or hatred, envied, hated, hateful, odious (i. q. invisus): etiam si is invidiosus ac multis offensus esse videatur,: damnatio,: triumphum accipere, invidiosum ad bonos,: in eos,: invidiosis nominibus utebatur consul,: invidiosa oratione multitudo credula accenditur,: laudatrix Venus mihi,. — Sup.: invidiosissimus,; ; — Hence, invĭdĭōsē, adv., enviously, invidiously; hatefully, odiously (class.): dicere,; ; ; .— Comp.: expulsus,.

la:noun:invidia.gloss: envy, grudge, grudging, jealousy, prejudice, spite
senses: envy, grudge, grudging, jealousy, prejudice, spite
odium, unpopularity, dislike, hatred, infamy, malice, resentment, ill-will
la:noun:invidia.html:
invĭdĭa, ae, f.
invidus
,
envy, grudge, jealousy, act. and pass.; cf.: ut effugiamus ambiguum nomen invidiae,: quoniam invidia non in eo qui invidet solum dicitur, sed etiam in eo cui invidetur,; (whereas invidentia is only act.; class.).
Act., envy jealousy, ill-will.—With gen. of person envying: invidiā ducum perfidiāque militum Antigono est deditus,: nobilium,.—With gen. of obj.: invidia atque obtrectatio laudis suae,: divitiarum,. More freq. absol.: invidia adducti,: invidiam sequi,: virtus digna imitatione, non invidiā,: invidia Siculi non invenere tyranni majus tormentum,; ; . —
Esp., in phrases: sine invidia, without ill-will, ungrudgingly: laudem invenire,: dare oscula,willingly, with pleasure,.—
Transf., an object of envy or illwill: invidiae fucinus,.—
Pass., envy, ill-will, odium, unpopularity: ne quae me illius temporis invidia attingeret,: in invidia esse,; : in invidiam invidia magna esse,: habere,to be hated,: reformidare,: in summam invidiam adducere,: extinguere,: in eum . . . invidia quaesita est,: invidiam placare paras, virtute relictā,: non erit invidiae victoria nostra ferendae, not sufficient to endure, i. e. not so great as to justify so odious a result, ; cf. : venire in invidiam,: invidiā onerare quemquam,: cumulare alicui invidiam,: conflare,: invidiae alicui esse,: invidiam a se removere,: sedare,: lenire,: pati,: intacta invidiā media sunt: ad summa

ferme tendit, : Ciceronis,the unpopularity of,: Caesaris,; : fraterna,: Decemviralis,.— Esp., in phrase: absit invidia verbo,to be said without boasting,; .—Plur.: vita remota a procellis invidiarum,; .

la:verb:invideo.gloss: to look askance or maliciously at, cast an evil eye upon
senses: to look askance or maliciously at, cast an evil eye upon
to be prejudiced against someone or influenced by prejudice
la:verb:invideo.html:
in-vĭdĕo, vīdi, vīsum, 2, v. a.
Lit.
In gen., i. q. βασκαίνειν (fascinare), to look askance at, to look maliciously or spitefully at, to cast an evil eye upon (only anteclass.).—With acc.: ut est in Menalippo: quisnam florem liberūm invidit meūm? Male Latine videtur; sed praeclare Attius; ut enim videre, sic invidere florem rectius, quam flori. Nos consuetudine prohibemur; poëta jus suum tenuit et dixit audacius,.—Absol.: ne quis malus invidere possit,produce misfortune by his evil eye, —
Trop., to beprejudiced against one, to be influenced by prejudice: semper dignitatis iniquus judex est, qui aut invidet aut favet,; cf.: cui nisi invidisset is, etc.,.—
Transf.
(I. q. φθονεῖν τινί τινος.) To envy or grudge one any thing.
With dat. of the person or thing exciting the feeling: malim mihi inimicos invidere quam inimicis me meis,: invident homines maxime paribus aut inferioribus,; : probus invidet nemini,: bonis,: invidet ipsa sibi,: Troasin,.—Pass. impers.: sibi ne invideatur,: illi, quibus invidetur,: invidia dicitur ... etiam in eo cui invidetur,: si is cui invidetur, et invidet,. — Of the thing: eorum commodis,: honori,; : virtuti,; : virtuti vestrae,: omnia tunc quibus invideas si lividulus sis,.—
Alicui in aliqua re: in qua (purpura) tibi invideo, quod, etc.,: in hoc Crasso,.—
Alicui with gen. of the thing (poet.): neque ille Sepositi ciceris nec longae invidit avenae,.—
Alicui aliqua re: non inviderunt laude sua mulieribus viri Romani,: nobis voluptate,; so with abl. alone: ne hostes quidem sepulturā invident,; : nec invidebo vobis hac arte, § 7: qua (ratione) nulli mortalium invideo,; cf.: si anticum sermonem nostro comparemus, paene jam quidquid loquimur figura est, ut hac re invidere, non ut omnes veteres et Cicero praecipue, hanc rem,. — (ε) With ob: ob secundas res malorum hominum, Sen. de Ira, 1, 16, 5. — (ζ) Absol.: qui invident, eorum, etc.,of envious men,; : qui invidet minor est,; : non equidem invideo,; ; : invidit Clytie,.—(η) Alicui aliquid (mostly post-class.; not in Cic.; cf. Krebs, Antibarb. p. 624 sq.): fama fuit Monuni Dardanorum principis filiam pacto fratri eum invidisse, Weissenb.: sibi laudem,: nobis caeli te regia, Caesar, invidet,: mihi senectus invidet imperium,; cf.: Liber pampineas invidit collibus umbras,i. e. deprives of, Forbig. ad loc.; cf. D. infra; : homini misero medicinam,: sibi voluptatem,; , ext. 1. — (θ) Alicui with object-clause: invidere alii bene esse, tibi male esse, miseriast,: nullus est cui non invideant rem secundam optingere,.— (ι) Aliquid alone, to envy the possession of, envy one on account of: oro vos id mihi dare quod multi invideant, plures concupiscant,: nam quis invideat mala,; cf.: haec qui gaudent, gaudeant perpetuo suo bono; qui invident, etc.,. — Pass.: ego cur, acquirere pauca Si possum, invideor? (for cur mihi invidetur) am I envied? .—Impers.: invidetur enim commodis hominum ipsorum,: non dixi invidiam, quae tum est, cum invidetur,.— Hence, P. a., invĭdendus, a, um, enviable: aula,: postis,; . —
To be loath, be unwilling; with a foll. inf. (poet.): invidens deduci triumpho,. —With abl.: invidere igne rogi miseris, to grudge, i. e. not grant a burning and burial, .—With inf.: his te quoque jungere, Caesar, Invideo,am not willing,.—
To emulate, aspire to rival: Caesar et se illius gloriae invidere, et illum suae invidisse dixit,.—
To hinder, prevent; to refuse, deny: plurima, quae invideant pure apparere tibi rem,: invidisse deos, ut Conjugium optatum viderem,; cf.: tene invidit fortuna mihi, ne, etc.,: Cereri totum natura concessit, oleum ac vinum non invidit tautum,: nobis invidit inutile ferrum,: nec famam invidit Apollo, .—With dat. and abl.: tibi laude, nobis voluptate,.— With abl. alone: ne hostes quidem sepulturā invident,: exemplo,: spectaculo proelii,: bona morte,.—Hence,
invĭdens, entis, P. a., envious: nocere invidenti,; ; : sive apud cupidos sive apud invidentes dicendum habuerit orator, —
invīsus, a, um, P. a.
Hated, hateful, detested (class.).
Of persons, animals, etc.: persona lutulenta, impura, invisa,: Cato,: suspectos alios invisosque efficere,: me invisum meo patri esse intellego,: invisos nos esse illos,: deo,: caelestibus,: divis,: Minervae,; : dominae deae,: infamem invisumque plebei Claudium facere,: ne invisi apud incolas forent, caverunt,; ; : (Helena) abdiderat sese atque aris invisa sedebat, Forbig. ed. 4 ad loc.; cf.: Tyndaridis facies invisa,. — Comp.: quo quis versutior et callidior est, hoc invisior et suspectior,.—Sup.: ipsi invisissimus fuerat,.—
Of inanim. and abstr. things: cupressus,: negotia,: dis inmortalibus oratio nostra,: regna dis invisa,: Troja jacet Danais invisa puellis,: improbitas judici,: potestatem invisam facere,: nomen Romanum ad aliquem,: omnia invisa efficere,: lux,: facies,: vita,: lumina,: aurum,: locus,: liberalitas,: Macedonum nomen,.—
In act. sense = inimicus, hostile, malicious (rare and poet.): invisum quem tu tibi fingis,; cf.: quae tanta licentia ferri, Gentibus invisis Latium praebere cruorem,: invisa belli consulibus fugiens mandat decreta senatus,.

la:verb:invenio.html:
in-vĕnĭo, vēni, ventum, 4, v. a. (
fut. invenibit for inveniet, Pompon. ap. ), lit., to come or light upon a thing; to find, meet with (cf.: reperio, offendo).
Lit.: neque domi, neque in urbe invenio quemquam, qui illum viderit,; ; cf. : in agro populabundum hostem,: Scipio mortuus in cubiculo inventus est,: naves reliquas paratas ad navigandum invenit,: tolerabiles oratores,: scis, Pamphilam meam inventam civem? is found to be a citizen's daughter, . —Sup.: pleraque inventu rara ac difficilia,; so . —
Trop.
To find out, to invent, effect: quandam fallaciam,: perniciem aliis, ac postremo sibi,.—Of an orator's faculty of invention: tanta in eo inveniendi copia et eloquendi facultas,: multa divinitus a majoribus nostris inventa atque instituta sunt, Auct. Or. pro Dom. 1.—
To find out, discover, ascertain, learn: inveniebat ex captivis, Sabim flumen ab suis castris non amplius milia passuum decem abesse,: conjurationem,: apud auctores invenio eodem anno descisse Antiates,; —
To find out, invent, devise, contrive how to do a thing: ille quomodo crimen commenticium confirmaret, non inveniebat,: Venus inveniet puero succumbere furtim,i. e. will find out a way, (8), 9, 35.—
To acquire, get, earn: ut facillume Sine invidia laudem invenias,: qui primus hoc cognomen invenit,: ex quo illi gloria opesque inventae,: laudem,; cf.: gratiam apud aliquem,.—
With se.
To show itself, appear: postquam se dolor invenit,.—
To be at home in any thing: minus se inveniunt,i. e. are perplexed,: nec medici se inveniunt,.

la:verb:investigo.gloss: to track or trace out, search after
senses: to track or trace out, search after
la:verb:investigo.html:
in-vestīgo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. (investigandum for investigandorum, Pac. ap. ),
to track or trace out, as a dog; to search after (class.).
Lit.: canum tam incredibilis ad investigandum sagacitas narium,: illam,: latentes conscios,: David et Viros ejus,.—
Trop., to trace out, find out, discover, investigate, search into: nihil investigo quicquam de illa,: quid dare velis, qui istaec tibi investiget indicetque,: nil tam difficile est, quin quaerendo investigari possiet,: qui sim, nequeo certum investigare,: Cibyratici canes investigabant et perscrutabantur omnia,: conjurationem,; : veri investigandi cupidus,: de Lentulo,: diligentia inimici investigatum est, quod latebat,: ubi Lentulus sit, investigare non possum,: conatus,: perquirere et investigare homines,: quae per notas scripta,to decipher,.

la:adj:invisus.html:
in-vīsus, a, um, adj.
Unseen: sacra maribus non invisa solum, sed etiam inaudita,: morbus,unknown,: invisus atque inaccessus in id tempus saltus,.—
Adv.: invīsē, without being seen (post-class.): invise advenerat,.

senses: to look after or watch over
la:verb:inviso.html:
in-vīso, si, sum, 3, v. a.
To look after, to go to see, to visit a person or place: ad meam majorem filiam inviso domum,: ad fratrem modo ad captivos alios inviso meos, Brix: huc intro ad me invisam domum,; : res rusticas,: quod Lentulum invisis, valde gratum, : eum locum,; ; : ut jam invisas nos,: Delum maternam invisit Apollo,: domos castas,. —
To look into: speculum,

la:verb:inveniendus.gloss: which is to be found or discovered
senses: which is to be found or discovered

la:adj:invitus.gloss: unwilling, reluctant, against one’s will, in spite of me, without my consent
senses: unwilling, reluctant, against one’s will, in spite of me, without my consent
la:adj:invitus.html:
invītus, a, um, adj.
perh. for in-vicitus; cf. Sanscr. va?*!-, to will; ava?*!as, unwilling; Gr. ἑκών, ἀ-έκων
,
against one's will, unwilling, reluctant (syn. coactus; class.).
Of persons: invitus me vides,: ut viatores invitos consistere cogant,: soli hoc contingit sapienti, ut nihil faciat invitus, nihil dolens, nihil coactus,: ego eum a me invitissim us dimisi,very unwillingly, very much against my will,: Berenicen ab urbe dimisit (Titus) invitus invitam,: trahit invitam nova vis,.— Abl. absol.: me (te, se, etc.) invito, against my (your, his, etc.) will, in spite of me, without my consent: vobis invitis,: si se invito transire conarentur,against his will,: Sequanis invitis,: diis hominibusque invitis,: invito numine,: invita Diana,: invitā Minervā, against one's natural bent, : invita Minerva, id est adversante et repugnante natura,: quod et illo et me invitissimo fiet,altogether contrary both to his inclination and my own,. — With ut: invitus feci, ut L. Flaminium e senatu eicerem,.—With gen.: credidit, dominum non invitum fore hujus solutionis,would not be ill pleased with this payment,.—
Of things: invita in hoc loco versatur oratio,: invitae properes anni spem credere terrae,: verbaque provisam rem non invita sequentur,: dantur in invitos impia tura focos,: lyra,: ignes,: oculis legere,; cf.: vultu prospicere,: ope,i. e. furnished involuntarily,: invito sanguine,. — Adv.: invītē, against one's will, unwillingly: invite cepi Capuam, (dub.).— Comp.: invitius,.

la:adj:invitissimus.gloss: unwilling, reluctant, against one’s will, in spite of me, without my consent

senses: to verbally attack, assail, upbraid, berate, rebuke, castigate
la:verb:invado.html:
in-vādo, vāsi, vāsum (invasse, ), 3, v. n. and a.
, to go, come, or get into, to enter upon.
Lit.: ignis quocumque invasit, cuncta disturbat ac dissipat,: consul exercitusque Romanus sine certamine urbem invasere,; : forum,: oppidum,.—
Transf.
To get into, fall into: ut profugiens hostem, inimici invadam manus, Att. ap. .—
In gen., to go, make, accomplish a distance: biduo tria milia stadiorum invasit,.—
To enter upon, set foot upon: tuque invade viam,: lutum minis frigidum,. —
To enter violently, move against, rush upon, fall upon, assail, assault, attack, invade (syn. oppugno); constr with in and acc., or simple acc.
With in and acc. (so nearly always in Cic.; cf. II. B. γ infra): in oppidum antiquum et vetus,: in transversa latera invaserant cohortes,: globus juvenum in ipsum consulem invadit,: in collum (mulieris) invasit,fell upon her neck,: alicujus pectus amplexibus,to embrace,: aliquem basiolis,; with osculari,: in Galliam,: si in eas (urbes) vi cum exercitu invasisses,: cum ferro in aliquem,.—Impers.: in oculos invadi nunc est optimum,.—
With simple acc.: aciem hastati invadunt,: stationem hostium,: validissimas Pompeii copias,: vicinos portus,: urbem,: jam tandem invasit medios,: eam (Europam),: regem,: in lecto cubantem,: greges,: madida cum veste gravatum,: ventus invasit nubem,: canes appropinquantem invadunt,: castra,; cf.: quem semel invasit senectus,.—Pass.: sperans, mox effusos hostes invadi posse,—Pass. impers.: signo dato, undique simul ex insidiis invaditur,.—
To rush into, enter hurriedly into a struggle, fight, etc. (poet.): Martem,: proelia,: certamina,: bella,: pugnam,; cf.: in pugnas, Lucil. ap. ; and: aut pugnam aut aliquid jam dudum invadere magnum mens agitat mihi,to attempt, enter hurriedly upon,. —
To make an attack on, seize, grasp: Jubae barbam,: cibum avidius,: pallium,: capillos, (4, 7), 5: virgineos artus,; cf. . —
Trop.
To fall upon, seize, take possession of, usurp; constr. with in and acc., or simple acc.
With in and acc.: in multas pecunias,: in quod ipsa invaderet,: in fortunas alicujus,; : in praedia alicujus,: in nomen Marii,: in arcem illius causae,. —
With simple acc.: dictaturam,: consulatum,: rempublicam,: imperium,.—
To make an attack on, seize, lay hold of, attack, befall a person or thing; with simple acc., or in and acc., or dat.
With simple acc.: cum gravis morbus invasit,: ne reliquos populares metus invaderet,: cupido Marium,; : tantus repente terror invasit, ut,.—
With in and acc.: dolor in oculos,: pestis in vitam invasit,: in philosophiam,: in nomen Marii,: vis avaritiae in animos eorum invasit,: vis morbi in corpus meum,; cf.: lassitudine invaserunt misero (mihi) in genua flemina,.

—

Rarely with dat.: furor invaserat improbis,; . —
Absol.: ubi pro continentiā et aequitate lubido atque superbia invasere,: ubi contagio quasi pestilentia invasit,: cum potentiā avaritia sine modo ... invasere,.—
To assail with words, accost (poet.): continuo invadit,: Agrippa consules anni prioris invasit, cur silerent,: Vinnium Laco minaciter invasit,.—Hence, invāsus, a, um, P. a., ingrafted: comae, i. e. rami,.
la:verb:invado.inflection: vāsi, vāsum, 3, v. n. and a.

la:adj:invidus.html:
invĭdus, a, um, adj.
invideo
,
envious (class.): neque ambitiosus imperator neque invidus,: invida me spatio natura coercuit,: Lycus,.—Subst.: invĭdus, i, m., an envious person, a hater: invidus alterius macrescit rebus opimis,; .—Mostly plur.: mei,: istos invidos di perdant,; : invidi, malevoli et lividi,: tui invidi,. — With dat.: o Fortuna viris invida fortibus,: aegris,.—With gen., envious of a thing: laudis invidus,: ille Martini non invidus gloriarum,.—Absol.: populus invidus etiam potentiae in crimen vocabantur—domum revocat,.—Also of inanim. and abstr. things: noxque fuit praeceps, et coeptis invida nostris,hostile, inimical, unfavorable,: invida fata piis,: fatum,: fatorum series,: cura,: et jam dente minus mordeor invido,: taciturnitas,: aetas,.

la:verb:involvo.gloss: to roll to or upon something
senses: to roll to or upon something
to roll about, wrap up, envelop, involve; cover, overwhelm; curl, coil up; veil
to involve or devote oneself to something
la:verb:involvo.html:
in-volvo, vi, ūtum, 3, v. a.,

la:verb:invideo#2.html:
in-vĭdĕo, vīdi, vīsum, 2, v. a.
Lit.

Nos consuetudine prohibemur; poëta jus suum tenuit et dixit audacius,.—Absol.: ne quis malus invidere possit,produce misfortune by his evil eye, —
Trop., to beprejudiced against one, to be influenced by prejudice: semper dignitatis iniquus judex est, qui aut invidet aut favet,; cf.: cui nisi invidisset is, etc.,.—
Transf.
(I. q. φθονεῖν τινί τινος.) To envy or grudge one any thing.
With dat. of the person or thing exciting the feeling: malim mihi inimicos invidere quam inimicis me meis,: invident homines maxime paribus aut inferioribus,; : probus invidet nemini,: bonis,: invidet ipsa sibi,: Troasin,.—Pass. impers.: sibi ne invideatur,: illi, quibus invidetur,: invidia dicitur ... etiam in eo cui invidetur,: si is cui invidetur, et invidet,. — Of the thing: eorum commodis,: honori,; : virtuti,; : virtuti vestrae,: omnia tunc quibus invideas si lividulus sis,.—
Alicui in aliqua re: in qua (purpura) tibi invideo, quod, etc.,: in hoc Crasso,.—
Alicui with gen. of the thing (poet.): neque ille Sepositi ciceris nec longae invidit avenae,.—
Alicui aliqua re: non inviderunt laude sua mulieribus viri Romani,: nobis voluptate,; so with abl. alone: ne hostes quidem sepulturā invident,; : nec invidebo vobis hac arte, § 7: qua (ratione) nulli mortalium invideo,; cf.: si anticum sermonem nostro comparemus, paene jam quidquid loquimur figura est, ut hac re invidere, non ut omnes veteres et Cicero praecipue, hanc rem,. — (ε) With ob: ob secundas res malorum hominum, Sen. de Ira, 1, 16, 5. — (ζ) Absol.: qui invident, eorum, etc.,of envious men,; : qui invidet minor est,; : non equidem invideo,; ; : invidit Clytie,.—(η) Alicui aliquid (mostly post-class.; not in Cic.; cf. Krebs, Antibarb. p. 624 sq.): fama fuit Monuni Dardanorum principis filiam pacto fratri eum invidisse, Weissenb.: sibi laudem,: nobis caeli te regia, Caesar, invidet,: mihi senectus invidet imperium,; cf.: Liber pampineas invidit collibus umbras,i. e. deprives of, Forbig. ad loc.; cf. D. infra; : homini misero medicinam,: sibi voluptatem,; , ext. 1. — (θ) Alicui with object-clause: invidere alii bene esse, tibi male esse, miseriast,: nullus est cui non invideant rem secundam optingere,.— (ι) Aliquid alone, to envy the possession of, envy one on account of: oro vos id mihi dare quod multi invideant, plures concupiscant,: nam quis invideat mala,; cf.: haec qui gaudent, gaudeant perpetuo suo bono; qui invident, etc.,. — Pass.: ego cur, acquirere pauca Si possum, invideor? (for cur mihi invidetur) am I envied? .—Impers.: invidetur enim commodis hominum ipsorum,: non dixi invidiam, quae tum est, cum invidetur,.— Hence, P. a., invĭdendus, a, um, enviable: aula,: postis,; . —
To be loath, be unwilling; with a foll. inf. (poet.): invidens deduci triumpho,. —With abl.: invidere igne rogi miseris, to grudge, i. e. not grant a burning and burial, .—With inf.: his te quoque jungere, Caesar, Invideo,am not willing,.—
To emulate, aspire to rival: Caesar et se illius gloriae invidere, et illum suae invidisse dixit,.—
To hinder, prevent; to refuse, deny: plurima, quae invideant pure apparere tibi rem,: invidisse deos, ut Conjugium optatum viderem,; cf.: tene invidit fortuna mihi, ne, etc.,: Cereri totum natura concessit, oleum ac vinum non invidit tautum,: nobis invidit inutile ferrum,: nec famam invidit Apollo, .—With dat. and abl.: tibi laude, nobis voluptate,.— With abl. alone: ne hostes quidem sepulturā invident,: exemplo,: spectaculo proelii,: bona morte,.—Hence,
invĭdens, entis, P. a., envious: nocere invidenti,; ; : sive apud cupidos sive apud invidentes dicendum habuerit orator, —
invīsus, a, um, P. a.

Of persons, animals, etc.: persona lutulenta, impura, invisa,: Cato,: suspectos alios invisosque efficere,: me invisum meo patri esse intellego,: invisos nos esse illos,: deo,: caelestibus,: divis,: Minervae,; : dominae deae,: infamem invisumque plebei Claudium facere,: ne invisi apud incolas forent, caverunt,; ; : (Helena) abdiderat sese atque aris invisa sedebat, Forbig. ed. 4 ad loc.; cf.: Tyndaridis facies invisa,. — Comp.: quo quis versutior et callidior est, hoc invisior et suspectior,.—Sup.: ipsi invisissimus fuerat,.—
